title: Filesystem search
subtitle: find, locate, and grep — which tool for which job

cards.meaning: Live tree by criteria / fast name DB / lines inside files
cards.notes: Memory hook: find = walk the tree. locate = phone book (update it). grep = search inside.

cards.meaning: Walk from / for basename exactly hosts
cards.notes: -name matches basename, not full path. Quote globs so the shell does not expand them.

cards.meaning: Owned by user / regular file / directory
cards.notes: Start narrow (/home, /var/log) — find / walks the whole machine.

cards.meaning: For each match, run rm with that path substituted for {}
cards.notes: \; ends -exec. One rm process per match.

cards.meaning: Print paths; xargs batches them as args to rm (fewer process starts)
cards.notes: Equal job to -exec for this course. Spaces in names need -print0 | xargs -0.

cards.meaning: Null-separated paths — safe if names have spaces
cards.notes: Default whitespace split breaks on spaces/quotes. Pair -print0 with xargs -0.

cards.meaning: Fast name search via database (can be stale)
cards.notes: Default DB: /var/lib/mlocate/mlocate.db. Does not crawl the live disk.

cards.meaning: Rebuild the locate database (usually as root)
cards.notes: New file missing from locate? updatedb then locate, or use find.

cards.meaning: Print lines that match a pattern (regex)
cards.notes: find/locate = which files. grep = which lines.

cards.meaning: Ignore case / show line numbers / recurse a tree
cards.notes: Pattern can be a regex. Combine later: find … | xargs grep or grep -r.
